Dead Cells is probably my favorite *whatever*. Metroidvania? Rougelite? Platformer? Its all three in equal measure, and it does a fantastic job of blending them together in a rewarding way that seems to keep the player coming back for more punishment. The gameplay will largely revolve around what build you want to play, and features a really fun system with three archtypes that you can either focus individually on, or blend at your discretion. This system rewards experimentation, and you'll be unlocking new items and abilities as you progress. Weapons, magical abilities, passive/active buffs, traps, companions, and the means of unlocking new routes thru the game. I really enjoy the way this game *works*. There's always a part in my reviews where I say something akin to "this game is eye candy", and I feel the same way about Dead Cells. Most of this game is visually stunning, provided you enjoy pixel graphics. Light is thoughtfully distributed throughout the dark tunnels, stretching corridors and dead keeps of the castle walls. Each of the "biomes" are visually unique, sporting bright and well placed colors that please the ape brain. This only reinforces the varying challenges that different routes can present the player. I'm a sucker for good parallax scrolling and this game masterfully uses multiple layers in some areas to make the land feel expansive and lived in. The story is probably the weakest part of Dead Cells, but I don't consider that to be a hard negative. While most of the "big reveal" is pretty upfront, there's a ton of hidden backstory and implications that revolve around the player character, the kingdom, and the king who ran it. I thought that was pretty fun, as I tend to enjoy *earning* my story breadcrumbs at a time. What I DON'T like about this is it means most people will never see the full picture, because they won't feel like completing this very challenging game upwards of 5 times, scrounging for flavor text and bits of lore along the way. All in all this is a fantastic (now unhidden) gem that finds itself in my rotation every few years. 8/10

I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of great games that are very clear and understandable In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends. Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

Going to update as I complete the game. Absurd input tracking/animation reading, non-stop attack chains from enemies, unclear map locations and side-quest unlocks (you will most likely need a guide if you're not trying to run around your entire playthrough). Most egregiously of all is the enemy chain of attacks which hardly leaves any frames for you to find to attack. Your spells hardly do anything useful past act 4. All while enemies are able to have constant chains that stagger you, and not only that but have immensely wide hitboxes while moving everywhere. The graphics/art is amazing yes we know, but the longer I've played this game the more repetitive it has felt.

好玩，但是总体来说有好有坏，首先，作为恐怖游戏来讲不算非常恐怖，其恐怖元素主要来源于阴暗氛围，和被追逐时的紧张，如果是一个人玩一段时间就会慢慢习惯，变得没意思，不过要是有朋友一起玩就好的多，好的点是很有新意，玩法上很有意思，通过找证据去判断鬼魂种类。但是想给官方一个建议，同时也给各位需要入坑的玩家一点提醒，这款游戏单人玩并不会有什么影响，但是想多人玩就比较依赖加速器，这个我们都能够理解，毕竟怎么说人家是外国游戏，但是卡顿和bug太多了，建议官方修一修bug，像有的时候一些道具bug，穿模bug，其次这款游戏在进行一些操作时前摇动作过长，游戏中鬼魂本来就属于会闪现的那种，让人本来就不好反应，再加上这种前摇超长情况，导致玩家很难反应，莫名其妙的突然死掉，还有就是转生系统，每100级都可以加一个转生，但是重置等级和金钱，等级重置我可以理解，作为老玩家来讲我理解用意，就是给我们这种老玩家一点新颖的体验，重回新手时期的难度，但是我不理解为什么重置金钱，我不去转生也是因为这个，毕竟我现在几百级，转生的话依旧是1转1级，也就是说不管你多少级重置以后相当于101级且没有钱没有道具，就算是做成重置等级金钱不重置也能接受，但是官方应该明白这个游戏有多难赚钱，建议官方改一下，转生以后变成一转等级减100，这种形式，让我们等级高的玩家转生不那么心疼，同时不重置金钱，可以参照等级扣出一定金钱，同时重置道具，这样感觉大部分玩家也可以接受，其次还有个别bug较为恶劣，比如有时候鬼魂猎杀时卡在墙里，和打火机明明是关闭的却有火焰还能正常使用，这种建模bug等等应该修复一下，其次就是很多鬼魂在特性上模拟其他鬼魂，甚至有点会出现自身没有的和不可能有的特性，非常影响游戏体验，导致判断正确率大大下滑，应该进行改正，还有关于摄像机和摄影机的画面显示bug，以前摄影机摄像机可以穿过门无风险拍东西，但是现在不行了，我能理解官方觉得不合理或者不平衡，修了，但是为什么有衍生出这么多的垃圾bug，现在的摄影机摄像机靠近门会黑屏，离远以后甚至有概率一直黑，无法使用，摄像机更是有时候出现镜头显示错误，出现一个大大的黑色十字，像是被胶带粘在镜头上一样，建议修改，这个会对我们造成极大的不良体验，所以各位玩家也是，想入坑也要可以接受这些bug，其次就是这个恶心人的新手指导，或者说没有一样，让你完全不知道该怎么玩，各位想玩尽量找人一起，或者随便进别的房间一起玩，游戏环境还是可以的，对新手都很友好，除了一些等级高不了多少又想装逼的，祝各位玩得开心，同时希望官方采取建议并做出相关改动，当然bug有很多，不一个一个列举了，希望我的评测会给你一点帮助

text: 好玩，好玩，这个11年的老游戏是我之前国庆促销买的，一开始是看价格这么低评分又这么高买的。虽然我完全是一个老滚5小白，完全没有玩过之前b社的游戏，也不太了解陶德什么的，但是玩了147个小时后依旧意犹未尽。画质很古老，不过是11年的游戏可以理解，繁体有点难受，不过有很简单的简体汉化mod，我也只是打了这一个，毕竟我算一个比较纯粹的游戏玩家，喜欢玩纯粹一点。战斗操作手法确实很没有打击感，也很不习惯，玩这么久也没有发现身体部位暴击什么的，比如打头没有暴击的感觉，当然也有可能是因为没有伤害数字什么的，只能纯看敌人血量条来判断。负重什么的很难受，不过也很真实，不可能一开始就有无限背包，要加耐力点或者专门的装备才可以提升。至于升级只给一点属性和升级慢也确实难受，不过游戏里有很多训练老师可以帮忙升级，不过要钱，技能等级升得越高钱要得越多，不过有一点很好玩的就是，有的技能训练师可以招募为随从，然后花的钱可以拿回来，可以白嫖。个人感觉最好玩的是偷窃这个技能，非常不可思议，当我把技能点满后可以对大多数npc扒光，让我对于偷窃这个技能有非常强的交互感。然后就是开放程度，虽然感觉地图很小，骑马一个小时差不多可以横跨地图（马也是真的慢，不过爬山确实好用，玩家和马简直是岩羊来的，是坡就能爬），但是npc的生活轨迹确实存在，这是现在大部分我玩过的游戏都没有的感觉，特别是好感度这个东西，现在大部分游戏的好感度系统是显性的，就是确实可以看见的，但是老滚5的隐性的，表现在拿东西这个方面，npc并不是只会在特定地方，而是有自己的生活轨迹（这点让人又爱又恨，因为找人确实有点麻烦）。最好玩的应该是动态的任务与实力系统，简单说就是没有等级限制和必须要完成的任务说法，虽然龙裔确实是主线，但是你不推也可以玩下去，我现在玩147小时只是推到要猎杀第一条龙的地步。很多看起来非常强的boss靠磨也是可以推过去的，并不需要要很好的武器或者准备什么的，我到目前为止最难的一个任务也是3小时磨过去的，不过后面等级上去，也快了很多。还有就是在游戏里的书是真的有用，虽然有的书看了会升技能导致我之前一直认为书只是升技能的，但是在我无聊看书的时候确实发现很多东西确实可以用，比如神射手这本书，还有附魔标准（应该是这个名字吧，有点记不清了），讲的东西确实都有用，还有一些书让我很惊奇，就是猩红匕首这本书，里面的人物并不只是传说，游戏里面确确实实是有相关人物的........还有太多太多给我惊喜的地方。总的来说，老滚5游戏手感还有画质差了很多，但是其他方面方放到现在依旧是一个好游戏。

I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of great games that are very clear and understandable In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends. Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord is a good game overall and one of the most interesting medieval sandbox games available. Building your clan, creating your own kingdom, commanding armies, and fighting massive battles can keep you entertained for hundreds of hours. The game offers a level of freedom that very few strategy RPGs can match. My biggest issue with the game is the lack of a co-op campaign. Bannerlord feels like the perfect game to play with friends. Imagine leading different clans in the same world, fighting together in battles, managing kingdoms, or conquering Calradia as a team. It is disappointing that this feature was never added, and I honestly believe it is the game's biggest weakness. I hope that if Bannerlord 3 ever gets made, TaleWorlds finally adds a proper co-op mode. Another major problem is smithing. The system is extremely unbalanced. You can start with around 5,000 coins and, after only 2-3 hours of smithing, end up with several million. This makes trading, workshops, caravans, and many other money-making methods feel almost pointless. The problem is that you cannot simply ignore smithing either. While you can choose not to use it for making money, you will miss out on some of the best weapons in the game. Crafted weapons can easily outperform most equipment you can find or buy, making smithing feel almost mandatory if you want the strongest gear. I also think the crafting system could be expanded. It would be great if we could craft armor, not stronger or unique armor, but simply the armor pieces that already exist in the game. Sometimes finding a specific armor set is a complete headache because of how random shops and loot can be. Being able to craft existing armor for yourself and your troops would be a great quality-of-life feature without hurting game balance. Another feature I would love to see is the ability to create custom troop trees. Instead of relying entirely on existing faction troops, players could design and equip their own units. Creating a unique army that reflects your kingdom's culture and fighting style would make the late game much more enjoyable and add another layer of customization. Combat is generally good, but some mechanics feel questionable. Crossbows not being able to penetrate shields feels strange. It is also a bit silly when a fully maxed-out warrior with a two-handed sword or axe gets his attack blocked by an enemy carrying a tiny wooden hammer. These moments can break immersion and make combat feel less believable than it should. The AI is decent, but nothing special. It is not terrible, but it is far from great. Sometimes kingdoms gather huge armies only to run around the map without accomplishing much. Instead of capturing settlements or defending their territory, they often wander around seemingly without a clear objective. One mechanic that I actually like is that axes and some polearms can cleave through multiple enemies in a single swing. It makes weapon choice more meaningful and gives those weapons a unique advantage. At the same time, it is disappointing that most other weapons cannot do the same. A massive two-handed greatsword should not stop after hitting a single enemy while an axe can cut through several soldiers. I think more weapon types should have access to this mechanic, especially larger two-handed weapons. Another thing that stands out is how much the game relies on its modding community. Sometimes it feels like Bannerlord is still alive because of modders constantly adding new content, fixing issues, and expanding gameplay. It is great that the community is so passionate and talented, and many mods genuinely improve the game. However, I think the developers should be doing more themselves instead of relying on the community to solve many of the game's shortcomings. A good example is the Diplomacy mod. Features from that mod should already be part of the base game. Managing a kingdom can become frustrating because you often have to chase NPCs all over the map just to talk to them. For example, recruiting a clan to your kingdom can turn into a long game of hide-and-seek. Diplomatic actions should be easier to handle, and some form of messaging system, diplomacy menu, or improved kingdom management would make the experience much smoother. As for multiplayer, it is mostly for a specific audience. Some players enjoy it a lot, while others will spend almost all their time in single-player. It is not bad, but it feels less popular and less interesting than the campaign experience. Overall, Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord is a very good game with excellent large-scale battles, a unique sandbox experience, and plenty of replayability. Despite issues such as unbalanced smithing, average AI, basic diplomacy, and some questionable combat mechanics, the game remains one of the best medieval war simulators available today. However, the missing co-op campaign is what prevents it from reaching its full potential for me. I hope TaleWorlds learns from Bannerlord's strengths and weaknesses and makes Bannerlord 3 a much better game. If they add co-op, improve diplomacy, balance smithing, introduce custom troop creation, armor crafting, smarter AI, and larger battles, I genuinely believe it could dominate the medieval sandbox genre for a very long time. I'm also looking forward to Chronicles: Medieval, which is currently planned for release in 2027. Competition is always good because it pushes developers to improve their games. I think Chronicles: Medieval has the potential to be a strong competitor to Bannerlord 2. However, if TaleWorlds addresses the major issues mentioned above in a future Bannerlord 3, I believe it would be on another level entirely and could remain the dominant medieval warfare sandbox game for years.

I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of great games that are very clear and understandable In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends. Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

The theme of the game is interesting, the idea of slowly building up a base from nothing a la skyblocks is really fun and cool! The story is very written very poorly and is very boring, the different islands you go are mostly bland and uninspired landscapes with very little details that immerse you in the game. Your base becomes a habitat full of administrative tasks that keep you running back and forth from chests to the thing you're working on and it doesn't feel great. The movement itself feels sluggish and like you don't quite exist in the world due to the floaty yet sluggish feel of the character and how they interact with the geometry in the world. I had a fun time but I left with a lot to desire upon completing the game. I think this idea will likely be taken by another team with a similar idea and elevate the experience, which I welcome as this game certainly has good bones but a poor presentation of everything else. 6/10 wouldn't recommend.

I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of great games that are very clear and understandable In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends. Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

game_name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
text: My all-time favorite game, but I can only give it one star I’ve put hundreds of hours into Skyrim across multiple saves. Two of my old playthroughs never hit the Chillrend sound bug at all, but my newest save finally ran into it, and it’s so frustrating. Chillrend has a looping frost hiss sound when drawn. This bug happens when the audio stop command gets lost during cell changes, loading screens or quick weapon swaps. Unlike Dawnbreaker or most enchanted weapons that only play a short one-off sound, this is a looping effect. Once it glitches out, the sound sticks to your character forever. Sheathe the sword, drop it, even delete it — the noise stays. It survives restarts and save reloads. Open a menu and it quiets briefly, only to come back right after. Pull Chillrend out again while the bug is active and you stack multiple layers of the hiss, which gets painfully loud. Since I play in third-person, I only noticed this Chillrend audio bug much later, forcing me to load a save from dozens of hours back and wasting days of my playtime. The vanilla workarounds are janky at best. Using `sexchange` twice or turning into a werewolf can temporarily clear the sound, but it comes back on reload. Worse, `sexchange` breaks the Ranger archery perk and removes its movement speed boost. There’s no reliable native fix in the base game. Trying to force-trigger the stop command by sheathing and teleporting at the same time only makes it worse and adds more overlapping audio. And it’s not just the Chillrend bug. The Creation Club homes are packed with well-known issues too. Weapon racks and plaques eat stored weapons, many display cases won’t accept gear. Dragon claws float off their mounts. Some adopted kids can’t move in, pets sometimes vanish or get sent to the wrong house. Mannequins lock onto one set of armor, push out any new gear you put on them, and duplicate that old armor when you leave the area and come back. Items jump all over the place every time you enter these homes, way more so than regular Hearthfire houses. Most display cases don’t work properly as displays at all. Serana also has her own annoying bugs. She will stop following you in basements and can disappear randomly. Her hood duplicates infinitely, stacking hundreds of copies in her inventory and making trading items impossible. On top of all these bugs, the base game volume is way too low. Compared to nearly every other game, even older ones like GTA V, Skyrim’s overall sound level feels like it’s only one third as loud. Every single time I boot it up, I have to crank my system volume. When I finish playing and jump on TikTok without turning it back down, the sudden blast of sound has startled me and even gotten me complaints from neighbours. I don’t want to sound harsh, but it’s unbelievable that pirated versions of Skyrim can run better with fewer bugs. The only extra thing this official version offers is the pointless achievement system. It feels like Bethesda just doesn’t care about polishing these long-standing quality-of-life problems. The community has to make mods to patch everything for them. Players end up doing the dev team’s job instead of just enjoying the game. It’s disappointing. GTA V is just as old, yet it feels polished and optimized. Meanwhile Bethesda chases big projects like Starfield. It’s like taking a warrior and forcing them to slog through boring, drawn-out religious texts. It is my all-time favourite game, yet also the buggiest. Bethesda is just as arrogant as Valve is with CS2. But my negative review reflects my real experience. I’m here to play a game, to enjoy something as a person, not to suffer and do your work for you.

母牛：“小明！你的被动好碍事啊！”小明先是一愣，然后马上就理解了母牛的意思，大笑着按了一下shift，说：“哈哈！尽管来吧！”母牛同样大笑着拍上了小明的肩膀，在他之后战甲们也不再拘谨，都带着轻松的笑容，为小明送上自己的祝福。“去吧！笨蛋帽子！”“去证明你不是靠优雅吃饭的男人”“如果很辛苦就换我上吧！”“要赢啊！小明先生！”“鲨客！！”有趣的是，因为缺少双腿的关系，ash只能坐着轮椅撞向小明… 面对浑身裂隙能量喷涌而出的小明，被誉为虚空之王的墙中人，恍惚感受到了犹如排山倒海般的压力【亿万年未有的紧张感再一次浮上心头】。小明的拳头毫不留情砸向拜勒斯（20级适应mod)，致命的红色数字亮起。仓促间用杀妈刀格挡的拜勒斯身体不禁后退，墙中人猛地回头，惊疑不定的表情充分暴露在小明面前。小明利用打出红色暴击（高达三位数的红暴)时进入的【自毁境界】（100万匹力量！！！)将自身状态拉满——暴击发出的一瞬间，平常需要刻意进行的裂隙能量操作都会变得如呼吸一般自然。那是仿佛除自己外的一切都围绕着自己旋转的全能感（实则是被抽陀螺了)。小明死死钳住墙中人的手腕砸向拜勒斯，两者交叠之际，第四发暴击如期而至。拜勒斯用身体护住墙中人连退十数米，借着短暂摆脱纠缠的时机，小明开始近距离吟唱咒词。“招笑”“技能强化”“避难所”——小明就已经抬手对准了天际。墙中人惊慌失措地喊出了拜勒斯的大名，下一秒，拜勒斯像喷气发动机般追放逐而去。眼看拜勒斯已呈败势，墙中人立刻出现，将目标锁定在移速缓慢的放逐上。既然停滞的必经之路挡着小明这尊大佛，那就用【超宏大爹】将放逐无效——无论无效哪一个，只要能阻止四技能能量攒够就可以了。墙中人的身体被小明一拳打歪，可卓越者全家桶还是奔向了天际的放逐，小明望着极速飞行的超绝dot发射器翠玉激光，叹息之墙冰盾，敌方地图炮火圈，逆天伤害火柱，超绝破盾棍母电球，逆天穿盾毒。再次吟唱：“招笑”“花里胡哨”“停滞”。墙中人瞳孔放大，一股寒气扑面而来。在被压缩的时空中，墙中人明白，自己再也没有任何机会阻止灾变的诞生了

我是P4G和P5R连着玩的 对我来说P4G就是一群高中生拯救伙伴打败大魔王的中二冒险故事，有一种纯正JRPG不用在乎太多细节设定，帅，爽，打就完事了，玩起来一路嘻嘻哈哈的就打完了 但是P5R这剧情真是从头到尾都让人想骂人 首当其冲的就是这个异世界导航APP，明明P4G里钻电视一样作为分割日常和异常的路径，P4G里钻电视却默认属于世界观的一环，不管怎么钻都没人会在意有人进了电视机不见了。但P5R这个异世界导航APP却不停地重复被人发现在马路上忽然消失作为剧情的爆点，不是哥们，你头一次被杏发现了还牵扯到女同学差点死了，结果就是不改，一大帮人天天在马路上玩消失深怕别人发现不了还不怕无辜路人被牵扯进去，明智丸喜都用发现异世界APP让人忽然消失和出现来察觉主角的身份显得主角这帮人真的就是一群弱智。 再就是明智这个小丑，早闻大名，真玩起来一开始以为是L这种角色，结果原来精神状态一直是最后一集的夜神月汗实在太小丑了，但更绷不住的是我听到双叶说“没有你的话，我就遇不到大家了！”，这是人说的话！？你生物妈死了就为你遇到好哥哥是吧，什么集美！？明智从头到尾都在嘲讽主角要杀主角组全家，结果主角组一直搁那“错不在你！你好可怜！我们原谅你！”衰我真在这让明智把这帮人全杀了灭了一次 狮童宫殿攻略完后，这剧情还算有点意思，社会意志不以个人行为转移，日本人选择了当鸵鸟无视狮童的犯罪事实，自欺欺人的相信强人政治只要狮童当选社会就能变好，自己又不愿意付出努力改变社会，霸凌排挤有清醒认知的人，和当代日本社会一模一样，本以为Atlas能有何高见，结果就是整个“圣杯”出来背锅，日本人变成这样都是圣杯害的！圣杯太坏了！草！ 想起之前玩破晓传说，轨迹系列等等JRPG，明明揭露了尖锐的社会矛盾问题，却简单的将问题归结在少数领导人或者某个敌人的阴谋，处理了这个“魔王”社会的一切不公，分配问题，阶级问题，种族问题就都解决啦！我可去NM的！没能力写政治戏和社会矛盾，那特么就别把这玩意写成主线啊，像P4G全程围绕救菜菜子谁关心一直在路边搞ZZ演讲的大叔在说啥。 路人学妹也是搞笑，P4G的玛丽我一直只当她是路人NPC，毕竟主线里真没啥戏份，但是这路人学妹强行给她加戏，最后2个迷宫又一点戏份不给，干脆和玛丽一样做成场外协助NPC不就得了，做成可操控角色又不让主线阶段使用，你是什么伙伴！？我认识你吗！？ 打完伪神尼玛的明智这小丑忽然冒出来给我吓一跳，原来P5R这逼死不了，恶心吐我了，直接卸载游戏视频站补完无印结局。

If you want a zombie game with parkour, just play DL1 (or The Beast).

One of the most fun games I've ever played, It isn't perfect as it can get very grindy in many place of the game, but the loop of hunting monsters, getting better gear to hunt stronger monsters, to get even better gear rarely feels all that tedious because every hunt feel just that little different to spice things. This game has beautiful sights, models and maps, a complicated but mostly intuitive menu system and genuinely good balancing and hit boxes. The story isn't anything to write home about but its interesting enough for a game that is essentially a boss rush with semi-open environments to explore and gather resources. with friends (as with many games) its even more fun, as the game is built with cooperation and coordination with a group just as much if perhaps a bit more then with solo players. Not to mention it have an extremely open and friendly community who are always ready to help new players. In addition to this the dlc expansion Iceborne is actually bigger then the base game and offers more of the same while adding more then enough to justify a new expansion and reward the skills you refined in the base game. if you want a well paced combat focused game that lets you turn your brain off or lock in depending on your mood, or just need something to mess around with your group for hours on end without much muss or fuss. Monster Hunter World is already the game for you. Buy Monster Hunter World:Iceborne, you won't regret. P.S: Stay away from the guardian armor set and defender weapons they completely ruin the base game's progression and you will be very frustrated when you get to Iceborne and suddenly you aren't tanking damage like you used to. They are basically for speed running to the DLC. I made this mistake and nearly rage quit on one of the early bosses in the DLC cuz I just wasn't as good as the game expected me to be due to being carried by Guardian Armor, or Defender gear.

One of the most fun games I've ever played, It isn't perfect as it can get very grindy in many place of the game, but the loop of hunting monsters, getting better gear to hunt stronger monsters, to get even better gear rarely feels all that tedious because every hunt feel just that little different to spice things. This game has beautiful sights, models and maps, a complicated but mostly intuitive menu system and genuinely good balancing and hit boxes. The story isn't anything to write home about but its interesting enough for a game that is essentially a boss rush with semi-open environments to explore and gather resources. with friends (as with many games) its even more fun, as the game is built with cooperation and coordination with a group just as much if perhaps a bit more then with solo players. Not to mention it have an extremely open and friendly community who are always ready to help new players. In addition to this the dlc expansion Iceborne is actually bigger then the base game and offers more of the same while adding more then enough to justify a new expansion and reward the skills you refined in the base game. if you want a well paced combat focused game that lets you turn your brain off or lock in depending on your mood, or just need something to mess around with your group for hours on end without much muss or fuss. Monster Hunter World is already the game for you. Buy Monster Hunter World:Iceborne, you won't regret. P.S: Stay away from the guardian armor set and defender weapons they completely ruin the base game's progression and you will be very frustrated when you get to Iceborne and suddenly you aren't tanking damage like you used to. They are basically for speed running to the DLC. I made this mistake and nearly rage quit on one of the early bosses in the DLC cuz I just wasn't as good as the game expected me to be due to being carried by Guardian Armor, or Defender gear.

Played The Witcher 3 more times than I can count. All the way back in 2015 on PC(GOG) and I’ve also completed it on PS4. When I heard about the remaster and the new DLC coming out in 2027, I knew I had to go back one more time. Having 100% completed it, I can now safely say this is easily one of the greatest games of all time. No one tells a story quite like CDPR and everyone should experience the Bloody Baron questline at least once in their life. There is truly nothing else like it. That said, the remaster isn't without it's issues. Visual bugs pop up, environments(especially indoors) can be excessively dark and performance takes a hit with ray tracing or path tracing enabled. In Novigrad, the framerate drops to nearly half of what it is elsewhere in the game. Going for all the achievements was also a headache, particularly with Gwent cards tied to NPC's that occasionally become unresponsive. These bugs have been around since day one and have never been fixed. Still, these are minor complaints for a game that remains pure joy.

I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of great games that are very clear and understandable In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends. Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of great games that are very clear and understandable In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends. Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

简短版（直接复制Steam） 推荐！独一无二的中世纪冷兵器沙盒。亲手带兵冲锋、骑枪冲刺的快感别的游戏很难替代。可以跑商、招兵、攒军团、攻城建国，玩法自由度拉满。 缺点：外交AI很迷惑，后期玩法重复，原版任务比较单调。 重点：创意工坊mod才是本体！ 打mod之后体验直接质变，喜欢中世纪带兵打仗的闭眼入。 ✅完整版 推荐✅《骑马与砍杀2：霸主》 时隔多年的续作，保留了骑砍系列灵魂：方向格挡冷兵器战斗、大地图自由沙盒，从一个小人物慢慢起家，跑商赚钱、招募士兵、培养同伴、攻城略地，最后自立为王，每一局的故事都不一样。 千人战场的氛围感很强，骑兵冲锋、步兵结阵、仰攻城墙，亲自下场厮杀的代入感一绝。锻造系统、家族声望、城邦管理，比战团的系统丰富很多。 但是原版短板也很明显： AI领主操作很迷，外交系统一言难尽，说开战就开战；大地图追人折磨，后期统一路上重复度很高，任务大多是跑腿；部分BUG、城池管理繁琐。 不过它有最强的救星——创意工坊！各种三国、奇幻、战争mod直接换一个游戏，可玩性翻几倍。 适合人群：喜欢中世纪、冷兵器、带兵打仗、沙盒自由玩法的玩家。 不适合：想要强主线剧情、精致剧情演出的玩家。 ✅玩梗短句版 骑砍2，原版是半成品，mod才是完整版！ 一枪冲刺，千军万马，从流民到国王，这爽感独一份。就是追领主追到崩溃，外交全靠随缘😂 你想要哪个版本？要不要我再写一个差评风格的？

游戏本身是相当不错的，很推荐给想要入坑这个游戏的新人朋友，当然这个游戏也有十分劝退的地方。 我主要活跃在移动与ns平台，并非steam。总游戏时长超700小时。 1.如果你只是把brawlhalla当作休闲大乱斗游戏（本质也是平台格斗），你可以玩得很开心（如果你有愿意和你一起玩的朋友）。但如果要体验它纯粹的格斗部分（特别是1v1模式），你将会被恶臭的环境（包括但不限于：嘲讽，被动，粪招复读）与惊人的elo机制恶心。 2.此游戏的服务器是土豆做的。大多数时候甚至挂加速器都无法稳定连上东南亚或日本服务器（这是距离中国最近的两个服务器）。 3.bmg在越来越多次的更新中，将游戏的平衡性做的很烂（主要是在1v1模式中），很多角色的攻击过于变态。 4.这款游戏的时间与学习成本是非常巨大的，上百小时才刚入门（这里同样指格斗技术方面的） 5.游戏对新手非常不友好。 总之，如果你只是想与朋友们（如果有的话）一起玩玩休闲大乱斗，你可以很快地在brawlhalla中寻找到快乐。但如果你想在格斗技术方面有所发展，你要做好吃苦与被恶心的准备。

Monster Hunter: World – 1,503 Hours Well Spent Monster Hunter: World was a huge turning point for the series. It brought Monster Hunter into a new era with modern graphics, a living and breathing ecosystem, seamless environments, and a much more accessible multiplayer experience. It also helped bring the series to a much wider audience around the world. I've spent over 1,503 hours playing this game, and honestly, I don't regret a single hour. What makes this game special is that even after almost nine years, it still has an active player base. I think that's a testament to just how good this game is. Not many games can keep players coming back for so many years. I also love the story and its memorable cutscenes. And the soundtrack deserves special mention. Some of the songs are genuinely touching and make certain moments in the game even more memorable. Monster Hunter: World isn't just a game I enjoyed playing; it's one of those games that leaves a lasting impression. 1,503 hours later, I'd still happily recommend it to anyone who wants to experience Monster Hunter.

TLDR: While the parkour remains excellent, nearly everything else feels like a step back from Dying Light 1. PROS: ➕Parkour is great ➕Story-driven choices that impact the narrative outcome CONS: ➖Enemy AI seems buggy and occasionally just “Shuts off” ➖Excessive pointless zombie spawns - literally 3 melee attacks suddenly spawns multiple fast infected ➖Sorting in inventory never saves ➖Narrative isn’t that interesting ➖Most quests are boring fetch quests ➖Obnoxious and constant audio cues that you cannot disable (constantly notifies of ANY nearby event) ➖Combat skill tree is boring My review for Dying Light (DL1) is here Content (Game world/Narrative) – [4/10] The game world takes place in a city called Villedor in 2036, 22 years after the events of DL1. The setting is mostly similar to Harran, the city from DL1. There are two main areas, a smaller village-like starting area that is a bit more rural, and the city proper, with larger buildings and a downtown-like area. Regardless of the differences, every building interior looks like every other and no matter how sheltered or locked down a place has been for decades, there’s always somehow zombies waiting for you inside. The exploration is good, and there are tons of random things to do in the open world. Think like an Ubisoft game, and all the good, and bad, that comes with it. The narrative to me was a big let down. You play as Aiden who is a “Pilgrim”. Basically what Dying Light has branded to be some sort of long-distance parkour enthusiast deliverymen. Aiden has come to Villedor to find his sister and thus begins the search. The story is just all over the place. I really like how there are (seemingly) big decision points to make, but these don’t seem to have a big effect on the story other than some slightly different cutscenes, dialogue, and the ending cutscene. I got about 20 hours into it before I was starting to get bored of the disappointing fetch quest side missions, and the main story itself. While there are some revelations near the end, the story never hit a positive note after dragging on. Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [5/10] The general gameplay loop is typical of an open world game - completing mission objectives from one area to another. Coming from DL1, there are some big changes, and most of them are not positive. The parkour remains the best part of the game, by far., and I think it’s improved a bit. Jumping from the top of towers still gives that white-knuckle tense feeling, so it’s still great there. Adding to the already good traversal mechanics are the paraglider and a grappling hook. Though DL1 had a grappling hook, it’s not bound to a talent, you get it about 60% of the way through the story. The night elements have also changed. Now, you have a timer that forces you to either use a consumable or reach a UV light before it runs out, else its game over. The RPG-like gear system has been expanded from just weapons to include gear. I didn’t find this very meaningful and the game could have done without it. Speaking of talents, there are two trees - combat and parkour. The combat tree I found terribly boring, but the parkour tree was good. The difficulty is more on the easier side. The few times I died were all because of failed parkour attempts and not the combat. Though with the combat, the Volatiles will still mess you up. The regular zombies are just a hindrance, and often annoying as the runners constantly show up when doing basic attacks against any enemy Technical (Graphics/Performance) – [5/10] I found the graphics to be this weird middle area between PS4 and PS4-era fidelity. The environments and world look great, if repetitive, but the character design and animations are a step lower. I played fully maxed and felt the performance was good. Of note is the constant bugs. I hear this has been improved with post-launch patches, but I still ran into things constantly. The most egregious is the enemy AI. The AI would occasionally literally “Turn off” and the enemies would just stand there. Also the Volatile chase sequences were a bit of a joke with how poor the AI is at following you 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSD Audio – [4/10] The music wasn’t great. In fact, I ended up turning it down because it was getting annoying. There’s also a sound effect, like sort of deep “Ding” that plays when an event near you is active, which happens all the time . I couldn’t find a way to turn it off, but it really takes you out of the game with the constant sound. The voice acting is good. Replay Factor (Longevity) – [6/10] There is NG+ and achievements. Perhaps the big draw would be co-op and the choices available within the campaign, even if they are a bit lackluster. Still, I think there’s some good replay value here. Final Verdict – [5/10] Dying Light 2 (DL2) simply isn’t a great game. It lacks something that made DL1 so special. If I had to attribute this downfall to features specifically, it would be the narrative, and the lack of nighttime danger. DL1 didn’t really have an amazing story, mind you, but the narrative here is just terrible. As I got closer to the end, it was a struggle to push on and finish when I just didn’t care about any of the characters or the ending. While I like the touch of adding major decisions to certain parts of the story, even the outcomes just weren’t exciting enough to push the narrative to anything above mid-tier. As for the nighttime danger, it’s sad because the game is literally called Dying Light . In the first game, nighttime often shifted the game from being an action game into a horror game. The tension and change were dramatic and noticeable. I never got the same feeling here. In DL2 night time is more of a stealth or parkour chase in the open world, or rummaging through samey-looking buildings due to the dangerous infected being outside. Even if you are spotted by a Volatile and a chase sequence begins, the AI is so dumb that it simply can’t keep up with the player. As long as you keep moving, there’s really nothing to fear. Just like DL1 though, the parkour continues to impress, and I do really like the traversal elements. But damn, if I only cared about the world at all. This is a hard one to recommend. As with most 5’s, I often struggle to recommend or not. In the end, I’m going to go with a recommendation. I love DL1, first-person games, RPG mechanics, and zombie games, so my love for the gameplay elements kept me interested enough to finish it, but barely. I would only recommend this if you loved DL1, and even then, prepare to be disappointed. Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] Yes $60 is steep. I wouldn’t pay over $15 for this game.
